name: danger-zone
description: The destructive action, set apart, behind a confirmation the reader has to type: the button stays disabled until the name is typed exactly, then writes the scheduled action to its record and says so in place, with a way to take it back until it runs.
provenPattern: Derived from a production account application: its auth shell, its destructive-action sections and its usage rows are the measured versions of these three arrangements.

knowledge.purpose: Keep an irreversible action reachable but impossible to take by accident
antiPatterns: A destructive button among ordinary settings — proximity is what makes a misclick possible
A yes/no dialog as the only gate; typing the name is what proves the reader knows which thing they are deleting
Describing the action without naming what is lost — “this cannot be undone” says nothing about what goes
An enabled destructive button before the name is typed — the typed name is the gate, so the button is disabled until it matches exactly
Demoting the title below h2 — the danger zone is a section of the page beside the settings cards, not inside one; its title is h2 (drawn small), so the outline never skips a level
A confirmation that leads elsewhere — the result is said in place, where the reader clicked, with the way to undo it next to it
Typing a name the page wrote by hand — the text to type is read from the record (CONFIRM_VALUE is an expression), so a renamed workspace is confirmed by its new name

mobileCollapse: One column: the warning, the confirm field, then the action last; once confirmed the field and the button give way to the result line and its undo.

placeholders.{{TITLE}}: heading.text — the action, e.g. Delete this workspace
placeholders.{{WHAT_IS_LOST}}: alert.message — what goes with it, named
placeholders.{{CONFIRM_VALUE}}: expression WITHOUT braces for the exact text the reader must type, read from the record so it follows a rename (e.g. settingsRecord.0.workspaceName), or a quoted literal (e.g. 'Example workspace')
placeholders.{{CONFIRM_LABEL}}: input.label — names what to type; it may be an expression over the record, e.g. {{'Type ' + settingsRecord.0.workspaceName + ' to confirm'}}
placeholders.{{SOURCE}}: id of the page source that holds the record the action changes (e.g. settingsRecord) — the server decides who may change it
placeholders.{{RECORD_ID}}: expression for that record's id, e.g. {{settingsRecord.0.id}}
placeholders.{{DO_VALUES}}: the fields the confirmed action writes, as an object (e.g. {"closingScheduled": true}) — the host carries the action out from that record
placeholders.{{SCHEDULED}}: expression WITHOUT braces that is true once the action is scheduled, read from the record (e.g. settingsRecord.0.closingScheduled === true)
placeholders.{{DONE_TEXT}}: alert.message shown in place once confirmed, saying what happens and when (e.g. Closing is scheduled for 30 Nov 2026.)
placeholders.{{UNDO_LABEL}}: label of the button that takes the scheduled action back (e.g. Keep the workspace)
placeholders.{{UNDO_VALUES}}: the fields the undo writes, as an object (e.g. {"closingScheduled": false})
placeholders.{{FAILED_TEXT}}: human message when the write is refused or fails — never the server's words
